title: 🔐 Linux Identity, Data States, Kernel Boundaries & Sterling Deployment
industry_title: Linux identity, data states and Sterling deployment

paras: Source-faithful reading, corrected interpretations, creative system maps, contradictions and cross-Atlas links.
Technical correction policy: detailed mechanisms, examples and verification in the corrections handbook
Interpretation: a service runs under an identity, while kernel mechanisms mediate resource access. An account is not a process; a daemon is a process, often with a dedicated service identity.

alice:x:1001:1001:Alice:/home/alice:/bin/bash username:hash:lastchg:min:max:warn:inactive:expire:reserved /etc/passwd: username, password placeholder, UID, primary GID, GECOS, home, login shell. /etc/shadow: nine fields: username, password hash or lock marker, password-aging and expiration fields. Hashing is not reversible encryption. NSS may retrieve network accounts through LDAP/SSSD, not just /etc/passwd.

id alice getent passwd alice sudo getent shadow alice ps -eo pid,user,group,comm Correction: system UID ranges are distribution-configurable, not universally 1–999; a service identity may have no interactive login shell; UID 0 is privileged root identity, not necessarily only an account named root.

The same library or artifact may be at rest in Artifactory, in transit over HTTPS, and in use when mapped into memory. Encryption at rest, encryption in transit and runtime isolation solve different threats.

Correction: Kubernetes volumes are mounts backed by diverse volume sources, not necessarily empty directories. A PersistentVolumeClaim requests storage; it is not automatically a backup or high-availability guarantee.

A shell parses and executes commands; it does not directly convert commands to machine code. Programs use syscalls (often via libraries). Linux containers share the host kernel; VMs have separate guest kernels. Namespaces isolate views (PID, network, mount, IPC, user); cgroups track and limit resources.

blocks.h2: 📦 Vendor image → customized OCI image → Kubernetes
paras: Vendor base image and supported extension paths depend on the exact IBM Sterling edition and release. Pin digest, validate signatures and licensing, scan dependencies, preserve the supported runtime UID, and do not place secrets inside images. Helm renders/manages Kubernetes release manifests; controllers reconcile workloads and node runtimes pull images.

kubectl create secret docker-registry ibm-registry \ --docker-server=registry.example.com \ --docker-username='<service-account>' \ --docker-password='<access-token>' \ --namespace=sterling Security: illustrative only; avoid credentials in shell history and use managed secret injection. imagePullSecrets are for image pulls, not necessarily application database authentication. ClusterIP is a Service virtual IP, not a Pod IP; Ingress requires an installed controller, and Gateway API offers another routing model.
